answers.answer: Rule is determined by comparing each player's total warriors plus buildings in the clearing; tokens and pawns do not count. An ordinary tie means nobody rules. The Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. The Vagabond cannot rule and does not prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle: Rule (2.5).

answers.answer: A normal move takes any positive number of the player's warriors or pawns along a linking path to an adjacent clearing, and the player must rule the origin, destination, or both. Rule is rechecked for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including in multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says otherwise.
answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle: Move (4.2).

answers.answer: The defender may play one matching ambush (birds are wild); the attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. The defender's ambush is discarded either way. If unfoiled it deals two hits immediately, not capped by defending warriors, and battle ends if no attacking warriors or Vagabond pawns remain. Resolve before-roll effects, then roll: higher die is attacker's hits and lower is defender's, with each side's rolled hits capped by its own warriors (Alliance reverses the dice; Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead). Resolve after-roll effects, then add extra hits without warrior caps and subtract ignored hits. A defender with no warriors makes the attacker deal one extra defenseless hit; for Vagabond this applies if it has no undamaged swords. Each side chooses its own removal order, but all its warriors must be removed before its buildings or tokens. Both sides deal counted hits; losing warriors does not change the rolled cap retroactively. Whoever removes an enemy building or token scores one VP each, even when defending or outside battle.
answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle: Battle (4.3), steps 1–6.

answers.answer: Crafting uses crafting icons at bottom left: activate crafting pieces matching those icons, rather than paying the card's suit. Each crafting piece can activate once per turn, except the Vagabond may reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. An item card cannot be crafted if that item is absent from the map supply. You cannot craft a persistent effect identical to one already in your play area.
answers.evidence: Shared movement, crafting and battle: Craft (4.1).

answers.answer: In your own Daylight, at 10 or more VP, activate a dominance card from hand, put it in your play area, remove your score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of your own Birdsong, mouse/rabbit/fox dominance wins if you rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if you rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. Meeting a condition earlier does not immediately win. An activated dominance card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: When a dominance card would enter the discard pile, put it near the map as available instead. During your own Daylight, spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into your hand. An available bird dominance remains bird, so it requires a bird payment; a bird hand card may pay for a non-bird dominance card.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: For two players, remove all four dominance cards before shuffling the shared deck; each player draws three cards. Place a ruin in each of the four R slots. Do not put items under ruins unless Vagabond setup hides one each of the four R-marked items there; without a Vagabond, ruins contain no items. Faction setup proceeds in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3–7; the Vagabond setup paragraph specifies hiding the four R-marked items.

answers.answer: Only the Marquise may place pieces in the Keep's clearing; other players may move pieces into it. When any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, Field Hospitals lets the Marquise spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of supply; this can apply outside battle. Without a Keep there is no hospital destination. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6): Keep and Field Hospitals.

answers.answer: In Daylight, the Marquise crafts first with workshops, then takes up to three actions plus one per bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit. March is one compound action of up to two moves, and you cannot interrupt it to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and may be used only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6): Daylight actions.

answers.answer: Choose a clearing you rule with an open building slot and a building type. Take the leftmost building of that type from its track. Pay the cost shown atop its column in wood from the target clearing or from other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP shown on the newly uncovered track space. The summary says a build requires the full wood cost, available building, and legal slot.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat (6): Build.

answers.answer: Birdsong proceeds: (1) Emergency Orders—if the hand is empty, draw one card; (2) Add to Decree—add one or two hand cards to any columns, with at most one bird card added; (3) A New Roost—if there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7): Birdsong, in order.

answers.answer: After crafting with roosts, resolve every Decree card in column order Recruit, Move, Battle, Build. The player chooses card order within each column; bird is wild. Recruit requires a matching clearing with a roost; Move requires moving at least one warrior from a matching clearing with normal movement rules; Battle requires a matching clearing containing Eyrie warriors and an enemy; Build requires a matching clearing the Eyrie rules, an open slot, and no roost already there. Each required action must be completed fully or Turmoil begins immediately.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7): Daylight and Decree requirements.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard all Decree cards except Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are available; then retuck the Viziers in the new leader's columns. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings. Daylight ends and the Eyrie proceeds to Evening, even after Turmoil: score the VP on the rightmost empty roost-track space, draw one plus uncovered bonuses, and discard down to five.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties (7): Turmoil, in order; Evening.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one hand card matching the clearing (birds count) to Supporters; a group move costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If the player has no matching card including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one deck card into Supporters. With no bases, the Supporters stack has a maximum of five and incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded; with any base it is unlimited. The summary does not specify further handling of this card when the stack is full beyond the stated capacity rule.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8): Supporters and Outrage.

answers.answer: Both happen in Birdsong, with Revolt first and then Spread Sympathy; each may be done any number of times. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on the Alliance board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit, and places one warrior in Officers. It scores normal VP for enemy buildings/tokens removed. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to existing sympathy, or any clearing if there is no sympathy; it spends the matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter if any one other player's warriors number at least three there (Martial Law). It places sympathy and scores the uncovered VP. It permits only one sympathy per clearing; Keep's placement ban still applies.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8): Birdsong, Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

answers.answer: Train in Daylight by spending a hand card matching a clearing with an Alliance base to place one warrior from supply in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay for Train. Organize is an Evening military operation: remove one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing to place sympathy there and score the uncovered VP; it uses no supporters and requires neither adjacency nor Martial Law, but needs legal token placement. When a base is removed, discard all supporters matching its clearing, including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and if no bases remain discard supporters above five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance (8): Losing a base; Daylight Train; Evening Organize.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed in that step adds no refresh then. Optional Slip moves to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, even into hostile warriors, and ignores effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. Normal Move exhausts one boot, plus one extra if the destination has warriors of any Hostile faction (including forced moves); it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest by this action, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. In Evening, if in a forest, Rest returns all damaged items to Satchel and flips them face up, but does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. The Vagabond always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on its track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3): Birdsong, Daylight Move, and Evening.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing, takes one hidden item face up into Satchel or a matching track, and scores one VP if an item is taken; remove the ruin when its last item is taken. Quest exhausts the two listed items for a face-up quest matching the clearing, completes it, and lets the Vagabond choose VP equal to matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards; no cards are spent, and a replacement quest is displayed. Repair exhausts a hammer and moves one damaged item to Satchel keeping its current face; ready tea, coins, or bags move to tracks if there is space.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3): Daylight Explore, Quest, Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction makes that faction Hostile immediately, except the special allied battle-loss rule. On the Vagabond's own turn in battle, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, excluding the warrior that first made that faction Hostile; ordinary building/token VP also applies. Infamy is not scored while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a marker out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it instead remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and does not give Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond (9; V.1–3): Relationships, Hostile/Infamy, Aid, and Strike.

answers.answer: The Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate dominance to coalition with a player not already in a coalition, choosing the lowest-VP player among all players other than itself (choosing among ties). It puts its score marker on that player's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including through dominance. A Hostile partner becomes Indifferent. Coalition partners are not enemies, and coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Vagabond coalition (9.2.8).
